problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where both $2\times 2$ blocks of $B$ represent rotation-scaling matrices:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-3+\text{i} \\ 5-2\text{i} \\ 2+4\text{i} \\ 3-4\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4-7\text{i} \\ 1-2\text{i} \\ 3+\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-5+\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-3\text{i},$ respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Invertible Matrix in Block Diagonal Form of an NxN Matrix

feedback.problem:
Consider the vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown below, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ represents a rotation-scaling matrix:

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4-\text{i} \\ -5\text{i} \\ 3-2\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 0 \\ -6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

The vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{3}$ are the eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ corresponding to the eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4+6\text{i}$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=-1,$  respectively. 
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ which of the following could be the matrix $P?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a real $3\times 3$ matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{3},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}={\overset{―}{v}}_{2},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}\text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{1}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{1}) & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {\lambda }_{3}\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ \text{Re}({v}_{1}) & \text{Im}({v}_{1}) & {v}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

From our block diagonal matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 0 \\ -6 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the first and second columns of $P$ will correspond to the complex eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and the third column of $P$ will correspond to the real eigenvector ${v}_{3}:$

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & -3 \\ 3 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$
